Hemi-methylation of the G1 GATC site during DNA replication generates a transient, heritable Psci1 promoter state that biases daughter cells toward opposing T6SS expression fates, thereby serving as the molecular mechanism for the observed epigenetic reversion of isolated ON and OFF subpopulations to the population equilibrium within 15–20 generations.

Wild-type EAEC outcompetes homogeneous ON and OFF populations during host infection in the presence of T6SS+ competitors because phenotypic heterogeneity at the sci1 promoter concurrently maximizes virulence and minimizes retaliatory mortality, thereby resolving the virulence-survival trade-off in a natural polymicrobial host setting.

The protective effect of T6SS-OFF cells against retaliatory T6SS+ competitors is mediated by physical shielding of T6SS-ON cells at the microcolony periphery rather than by simple frequency-dependent dilution, such that spatially intermixed microcolonies of ON and OFF cells exhibit higher population survival than segregated clusters of equivalent overall composition.

Transient hemi-methylation of the Psci1 promoter generates a functionally distinct intermediate subpopulation that assembles the T6SS more rapidly than OFF cells upon competitor contact while remaining less susceptible to retaliatory killing than fully ON cells.

In the mammalian gut, the epigenetic equilibrium of the EAEC sci1 promoter shifts to a lower T6SS ON-cell ratio than the 60:40 balance observed under iron-limiting laboratory conditions, because host innate immune defenses and interbacterial T6SS retaliation impose frequency-dependent costs that select for reduced T6SS deployment during colonization.

Clinical EAEC isolates from T6SS-rich communities harbor Psci1 promoter variants that bias the epigenetic ON/OFF equilibrium toward larger OFF subpopulations, reducing retaliatory killing costs while preserving a basal ON fraction for competitor suppression.

Killing of susceptible competitors by the EAEC sci1 T6SS releases iron that activates Fur-mediated repression of the sci1 promoter, driving epigenetic switching of attacker cells from the ON to the OFF state and thereby establishing a self-limiting negative feedback loop that stabilizes phenotypic heterogeneity upon competitor clearance.

In spatially structured polymicrobial communities, EAEC T6SS ON cells self-organize at the biofilm periphery to maximize contact-dependent antagonism, while OFF cells localize to interior regions where they buffer the population against retaliatory T6SS killing and maintain the epigenetically heritable equilibrium required for long-term population persistence.
moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code: The internal P4532 promoter within the sci1 T6SS cluster is bistable under iron limitation and controls heterogeneous expression of the downstream Tli1 immunity protein, generating subpopulations with distinct survival during retaliatory T6SS attack.

In polymicrobial communities containing both susceptible and retaliatory T6SS-positive competitors, EAEC fitness is maximized at an intermediate T6SS ON/OFF ratio that decreases as the proportion of retaliatory competitors increases, and epigenetically tunable wild-type populations outcompete locked ON or OFF mutants under fluctuating competitor composition.

EAEC dynamically shifts the equilibrium ratio of T6SS-ON to T6SS-OFF cells in response to the local frequency of T6SS-armed retaliatory competitors, biasing the population toward the OFF state to reduce reciprocal mortality while preserving sufficient ON cells for competitive killing.

Within mixed-species biofilms, EAEC T6SS-OFF cells are spatially enriched at microcolony interfaces adjacent to T6SS-positive retaliatory competitors, and this self-organized patterning further enhances population survival compared with homogeneous ON or OFF populations.

In structured biofilms containing T6SS-positive retaliatory competitors, EAEC enriches T6SS-OFF cells at the colony periphery, forming a protective buffer that reduces retaliatory killing and enhances overall population survival relative to spatially unstructured mixtures.

The internal P4532 promoter exhibits Fur- and Dam-dependent bistability that controls T6SS sheath assembly independently of Psci1, such that mutating its GATC methylation sites or Fur box converts the population to a homogeneous assembly state without altering overall Sci1 protein abundance.

EAEC populations exposed to periodically fluctuating iron availability will achieve greater competitive fitness when their endogenous Sci1 T6SS ON/OFF switching rate matches the frequency of iron shifts, with mismatched switching mutants showing reduced survival against retaliatory T6SS competitors.

The EAEC sci1 T6SS ON/OFF equilibrium shifts toward a lower proportion of ON cells when co-cultured with T6SS-armed retaliatory competitors relative to T6SS-deficient competitors, reflecting frequency-dependent selection that tunes the epigenetic Fur-Dam switch.

Increasing the density of T6SS-armed retaliatory competitors in polymicrobial communities selects for a lower optimal fraction of EAEC T6SS-ON cells, as the nonlinear survival cost of retaliation outweighs the benefit of competitor killing at high rival density.

The proportion of T6SS-ON cells in EAEC populations is actively tuned by environmental feedback, such that co-culture with T6SS-armed competitors enriches the OFF subpopulation while co-culture with susceptible competitors enriches the ON subpopulation, thereby optimizing population fitness across fluctuating polymicrobial communities.
